question.text: Ganga Debt AIF draws INR 100 crore at t=0. At end of Y7, it distributes INR 200 crore (single terminal distribution; no interim). Ignoring fees, Gross IRR over 7 years is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Solve 100 = 200/(1+IRR)^7: (1+IRR)^7 = 2.0; 1+IRR = 2^(1/7) = 1.1041; IRR ≈ 10.41%. This follows the single outflow/inflow gross-IRR formula in the workbook. The Trap: 14.30% is for 2x in 5 years. 7.17% is for 2x in 10 years. 100% is absolute ROI but not annualised. Note: The workbook defines IRR as an annualised cash-flow return; absolute ROI is not the same as IRR.
